title: Wavelength: Optical Interconnect for High-Performance Computing
problem: Electrical interconnects in HPC clusters face bandwidth density limitations that constrain cluster communication performance. Current switching fabrics cannot efficiently support the communication demands of modern high-performance computing systems.
motivation: Optical interconnects can significantly increase bandwidth density and improve overall cluster performance by leveraging wavelength-division multiplexing.
method: Wavelength proposes an optical interconnect fabric using wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) to multiplex multiple data streams over optical fibers. The design enables simultaneous transmission of different wavelengths on the same physical fiber, increasing effective bandwidth. The fabric architecture connects HPC cluster nodes through optical switches and transceivers rather than traditional electrical interconnects.
key_novelty: Application of wavelength-division multiplexing to create a practical optical interconnect fabric achieving 10x higher bandwidth density than electrical alternatives.
contributions: Optical interconnect fabric design using wavelength-division multiplexing
10x bandwidth density improvement over electrical interconnects
Practical implementation for HPC cluster communication
